answer: Each epoch, a garden of 150 plots hides opal stones ($12 each) fired in a forge kiln at 1,200°C, each crack pattern unique, registered. An agent gets one plot at epoch start, walks the garden, and photographs their opal with GPS and a timestamp as proof of presence. The kiln log records every firing, so a copied stone fails the pattern match. Forging 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 opals ($12,000), 20 kiln batches at $400 ($8,000), and 1,000 garden visits at $30 a trip ($30,000), over $50,000 per epoch. A garden blooms only for hands that dug in it; this registry trusts only feet that walked it.
